name: Omeprazole
route_note: Oral delayed-release capsules or tablets once or twice daily before a meal; IV in some countries
owner: generic (many); AstraZeneca (Rx brand), Procter & Gamble (Prilosec OTC)

discovery.by: Astra Hässle (team including Ivan Östholm, Lars Olbe and Enar Carlsson)
discovery.note: A substituted benzimidazole optimised from timoprazole to inhibit the gastric H+/K+ ATPase.

rx_status: prescription; OTC for heartburn in many countries
tagline: The first proton pump inhibitor, transforming treatment of ulcers and reflux
summary: Omeprazole is the first proton pump inhibitor, a class that irreversibly blocks the final step of gastric acid secretion. It is used for peptic ulcers, gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and Helicobacter pylori eradication, and in the late 1990s it was the world's best-selling drug.
mechanism: Omeprazole is a prodrug that accumulates in the acidic secretory canaliculi of parietal cells, where it is converted to a reactive sulfenamide.

The sulfenamide forms covalent disulfide bonds with cysteine residues of the H+/K+ ATPase (proton pump), irreversibly inhibiting it. Acid secretion recovers only as new pumps are synthesised, so a single daily dose suppresses acid for longer than the drug's short plasma half-life.
uses: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and erosive oesophagitis

history.title: Launch
history.detail: Losec is launched in Sweden and Europe.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: FDA approves omeprazole; the US name changes from Losec to Prilosec in 1990 to avoid confusion with Lasix.

history.title: Top-selling drug
history.detail: By the late 1990s Losec is the world's best-selling medicine.

history.title: OTC in the US
history.detail: Prilosec OTC is approved for frequent heartburn.

history.title: Fracture warning
history.detail: FDA warns of possible hip, wrist and spine fractures with high-dose or long-term PPIs.

history.title: Hypomagnesaemia
history.detail: FDA warns that long-term PPI use can cause low magnesium.

history.title: C. difficile
history.detail: FDA warns of an increased risk of Clostridioides difficile diarrhoea with PPIs.

facts: Esomeprazole is the S-enantiomer of omeprazole.
CYP2C19 poor metabolisers have several-fold higher omeprazole exposure.
